children: Natural Universals and the Global Scale
自然普遍性与全球尺度
To see a World in a Grain of Sand
And a Heaven in a Wild Flower,
Hold Infinity in the palm of your hand
从一粒沙中看见一个世界，
从一朵野花中看见一个天堂，
——选自威廉·布莱克《纯真的预言》（“Auguries of Innocence”）

Generalization. The action or process of generalizing, i.e. of forming, and expressing in words, general notions or propositions obtained from the observation and comparison of individual facts or appearances; also, an instance of this.
概括的行动或过程，即从对个别事实或现象的观察与比较中形成并用词语表达一般概念或命题；也指这一过程的一个实例。

Many things are said to be universal: freedom, money, love. But the two most historically successful universal claims—which continue to form exemplars for all universality—are still God and Nature. The universality of God and the universality of Nature are historically connected; in the European Renaissance, the stirrings of modern science conceived the latter on the model of the former. Only because God was known to be universal could Nature be depicted that way. The connection between God and Nature has continued to inspire the musings of theologians, scientists, and naturalists, reminding us of the importance of reason and mystery in appreciating each domain. Yet readers interested in how God came to be universal will have to consult other texts. This chapter enters the story midway to ask about the universality of capital-N Nature, that is, the awe-inspiring, lawlike systematicity of the cosmos and of life on earth.

许多东西被说成普遍的：自由、金钱、爱。但历史上最成功的两个普遍性主张——它们继续成为一切普遍性的典范——仍然是上帝与自然。上帝的普遍性与自然的普遍性在历史上相连；在欧洲文艺复兴中，现代科学的萌芽以前者为模型构想后者。只有因为上帝被认知为普遍的，自然才能被那样描绘。上帝与自然之间的联系继续激发神学家、科学家和博物学家的沉思，提醒我们理性与神秘在欣赏各自领域时的重要性。然而，对上帝如何变得普遍感兴趣的读者，将不得不查阅其他文本。本章从故事中途进入，询问大写N的自然（Nature）的普遍性，即宇宙与地球生命令人敬畏的、法则般的系统性。

Nature and the globe have helped make each other. Today’s most powerful claims about the nature of the globe refer us to global Nature: If universal laws of Nature can be established, then the globe forms an orderly part of them. The globe is a node for the expression of universal logic. Scalemaking, in turn, is a foundational move in establishing the neutrality and universalism of Nature; only if observations are compatible and collapsible across scales can they be properly described by a universal logic. Yet to “think globally” is no easy task. To recognize the globe as the relevant unit for our imaginations requires work. Moreover, establishing Nature has never been simple.
自然与地球帮助彼此形成。今天关于地球本质最有力的主张把我们引向全球自然：如果自然的普遍法则可以被确立，那么地球就是它们的有序部分。地球是普遍逻辑表达的一个节点。反过来，尺度制造是确立自然的中立性与普遍主义的一个基础性举措；只有观察在不同尺度之间相容且可相互归并，它们才能被普遍逻辑恰当描述。然而“放眼全球地思考”并非易事。要把地球认识为想象的相关单位，需要付出努力。此外，确立自然从来都不简单。

How does the universality of Nature operate in a world of friction? I approach this question through looking at the process of “generalization,” in which small details support great visions and the universal is discovered in particularities. Two features of generalization intrigue me. First, generalization to the universal requires a large space of compatibility among disparate particular facts and observations. As long as facts are apples and oranges, one cannot generalize across them; one must first see them as “fruit” to make general claims. Compatibility standardizes difference. It allows transcendence: the general can rise above the particular. For this, compatibility must pre-exist the particular facts being examined; and it must unify the field of inquiry. The searcher for universal truths must establish an axiom of unity—whether on spiritual, aesthetic, mathematical, logical, or moral principles.

在充满摩擦的世界中，自然的普遍性如何运作？我通过考察“概括”过程来接近这个问题，在这个过程中，小细节支持宏大的愿景，普遍性在特殊性中被发现。概括的两个特征让我着迷。第一，向普遍的概括需要在不同特殊事实与观察之间存在一个大的兼容空间。只要事实是苹果和橘子，就不能跨越它们进行概括；必须先把它们看作“水果”，才能提出一般主张。兼容性使差异标准化。它允许超越：一般可以凌驾于特殊之上。为此，兼容性必须存在于被考察的特殊事实之前；它必须统一探究的场域。普遍真理的寻求者必须确立一条统一公理——无论是基于精神的、审美的、数学的、逻辑的还是道德的原则。

Second, tentative and contingent collaborations among disparate knowledge seekers and their disparate forms of knowledge can turn incompatible facts and observations into compatible ones. Just as tiny convergences in incompatible testimonies at a criminal trial can establish a line of truth, the founding lines through which we learn to recognize Nature are often established in convergent opinions. Convergences offer legitimacy and charisma to nascent categories. They offer bridges over unrecognizable difference. Convincing universals must be able to travel with at least some facility in the world, and this requires negotiations across incompatible difference. Upon occasion, these give rise to collaboratively agreed upon Natural objects. The unfamiliar becomes the familiar through this process, and generalization can occur.

第二，不同知识寻求者及其不同知识形式之间试探性的、偶然的合作，可以把不相容的事实与观察变成相容的。正如刑事审判中不相容证词之间的微小趋同可以确立一条真相线索，我们借以学会辨认自然的奠基性线索，常常是在趋同的意见中确立的。趋同为新生的范畴提供合法性与感召力。它们在无法辨认的差异之上架起桥梁。有说服力的普遍性必须至少能够较为顺畅地在世界上传播，而这需要跨越不相容差异的协商。有时，这些协商会产生合作商定的自然对象。陌生者通过这一过程变成熟悉者，概括得以发生。

What is most striking to me about these two features of generalization is the way they cover each other up. The specificity of collaborations is erased by pre-established unity; the a priori status of unity is denied by turning to its instantiation in collaborations. Buoyed by axioms of unity, collaborations create convincingly agreed upon observations and facts that then appear to support generalization directly, that is, without the prior mediation of the collaboration. The contingency of the collaboration, and its exclusions, no longer seem relevant because the facts come to “speak for themselves.” ‘The pre-evidential status of the axiom of unity fades into the background, too, when facts naturalized through collaboration can be called on as the natural basis of generalization.

让我最震惊的是这两个概括特征的相互遮蔽方式。合作的特殊性被预先确立的统一性抹除；统一性的先验地位则通过转向其在合作中的实例化而被否认。在统一性公理的支撑下，合作创造出令人信服地商定的观察与事实，这些观察与事实随后显得直接支持概括，也就是说，无需合作的先在中介。合作的偶然性及其排斥似乎不再相关，因为事实开始“自己说话”。当通过合作自然化的事实可以被援引为概括的自然基础时，统一性公理的先于证据的地位也退入背景。

Generalization to the universal is at the heart of much analytic work; it makes it possible to devise market principles from particular transactions, to interpret events within Biblical prophecy, to mobilize class struggle, and to make scientific observations speak to general laws. No one I know wants to accept every claim made through generalization—or to dismiss them all out of hand. To characterize the process of generalization is not to reject all its products. I am not making fun of this procedure in studying it; I have no interest in ironic dismissals. I write here only about generalizations that I care about.
对普遍的概括是许多分析工作的核心；它使从具体交易中设计市场原则、在圣经预言中解释事件、动员阶级斗争，以及让科学观察支持一般法则成为可能。我认识的没有人愿意接受通过概括提出的每一个主张——或者不加考虑地将它们全盘否定。描述概括的过程并不是拒绝它的所有产物。我研究这一程序并不是在取笑它；我对反讽式的否定没有兴趣。我在这里只写我关心的那些概括。

In this chapter, I illustrate the interplay of the two processes of generalization I have introduced in defining the global scale together with universal Nature. For this, I have chosen discrepant examples: the emergence of botanical science, American nature loving, mathematical climate modeling, and an international forestry accord. Each offers a different axiom of unity through which individual observations are made available for generalization. Botanical science first generalized on the basis of God’s will, and only later substituted evolutionary process. American nature loving proposed a spiritual and aesthetic unity for Nature. Climate modeling has offered systems logic. Forest management advocates turned to international politics. Each project, in turn, has built from a divergent history of collaborative relations, such as those that connect botanical collectors across the world, or link nature lovers and promoters of tourism, or join scientists and policy makers. I show how these contingent collaborations are necessary to the process of generalization even as they are covered up by it. Axioms of unity and collaborations both need each other and hide each other; generalization—with its particularistic exclusions and biases—is produced as the product of this interaction.

在本章中，我通过四个相异的例子，说明我引入的两种概括过程如何在定义全球尺度与普遍自然时相互作用：植物科学的兴起、美国人对自然的热爱、数学气候建模和一项国际森林协定。每个例子都提供一种不同的统一性公理，个别观察借此可供概括。植物科学首先以上帝的意志为基础进行概括，后来才代之以演化过程。美国自然之爱为自然提出了一种精神与审美的统一。气候建模提供了系统逻辑。森林管理的倡导者转向国际政治。每个项目又各自建立在不同的合作历史之上，例如连接世界各地植物采集者的关系，或连接自然爱好者与旅游推广者的关系，或连接科学家与政策制定者的关系。我要说明这些偶然合作如何是概括过程所必需的，即使它们被这一过程所掩盖。统一性公理与合作彼此需要，也彼此隐藏；概括——连同其特殊主义的排斥与偏见——作为这种互动的产物被生产出来。
[T]he world is a great library, and Fruit trees are some of his Bookes wherein we may read and see plainly the Attributes of God his Power, Wisdom, Goodness, etc.
世界是一座大图书馆，果树是他的书中的几本，在其中我们可以阅读并清楚地看到上帝的属性——力量、智慧、善等等。
—R. Austen, The Spiritual Use of an Orchard
——R. 奥斯汀，《果园的精神用途》（The Spiritual Use of an Orchard）

Botanical classification had a privileged role at the beginning of modern science. Botany pioneered understandings of Nature, showing the potential of a universal science. Botany was perhaps the first science concerned with uniting knowledge from around the globe to create a singular global knowledge. The global scale and the universal were developed and demonstrated for science in this emergent field.
植物分类学在现代科学开端拥有特殊地位。植物学开创了对自然的理解，展示了普遍科学的潜力。植物学也许是第一门致力于把来自全球的知识联合成单一全球知识的科学。全球尺度与普遍性在这门新兴学科中为科学而发展并得到展示。

European voyages of discovery in the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries stimulated interest in the diversity of plants around the world. The folk botanies of Europe could not incorporate the wealth of unfamiliar plants that were being described from Asia, Africa, and the New World. In the ensuing excitement about new plants, a universal logic was put forward for the task of ordering global diversity: the logic of God’s creation. Plants formed a unified set because God had created them according to His plan. The insight of botanical science was to imagine from this plan a universal system of classification. In the nineteenth century, the strength of the system allowed insights about an evolutionary history linking organisms, and only then did a logic within Nature usurp God as the unifying source of order of global biology. But by then, plant classification had begun its descent to the lowly scholarly status it occupies today: data collection. Today, newly discovered plants are members of a pre-established scientific set: the plant kingdom, with its constituent families, genera, and species. They are self-evident elements of Nature and thus of little abstract interest. This success in reducing mysteries to facts speaks to the transformation of consciousness involved in making universality, and the global scale, self-evident. Botanical classification was an important catalyst for this transformation.

15、16世纪欧洲的发现航行激发了对世界各地植物多样性的兴趣。欧洲的民间植物学无法纳入那些从亚洲、非洲和新世界被描述的大量陌生植物。在对新植物的兴奋中，一种普遍逻辑被提出来承担整理全球多样性的任务：上帝创造的逻辑。植物构成一个统一集合，因为上帝按照他的计划创造了它们。植物科学的洞见在于从这一计划想象出一个普遍的分类系统。19世纪，该系统的力量使人们得以洞见连接生物体的演化史，直到那时，自然内部的逻辑才取代上帝成为全球生物秩序的统一来源。但到那时，植物分类学已开始下降到它今天所处的低微学术地位：数据收集。今天，新发现的植物是预先确立的科学集合——植物界及其所属的科、属、种——的成员。它们是自然的自明元素，因此没有多少抽象趣味。把神秘简化为事实的成功，说明了使普遍性和全球尺度变得自明所涉及的意识转变。植物分类学是这一转变的重要催化剂。

A key feature of this transformation was the erasure of the collaborations that made global knowledge possible. European botanical knowledge in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries was gained by learning from Asians, Africans, and indigenous Americans who introduced Europeans to their native plants. Botanical treatises from this period acknowledge the centrality of these knowledge exchanges. As European power grew around the world, however, European botanists came increasingly to imagine themselves as communing directly with plants—and the universality of science—without the mediation of non-European knowledge. The very collaborations that had made this science possible were covered up, and the plants were asked to speak for themselves as elements of Nature. In the history of systematics (the science of classification), universal premises and collaboratively established facts hid each other’s work. Given its importance in establishing Nature, it is worth elaborating this story in a little more detail.

这一转变的一个关键特征是抹除使全球知识成为可能的合作。16、17世纪欧洲的植物学知识，是通过向亚洲人、非洲人和美洲原住民学习而获得的，他们向欧洲人介绍了自己的本土植物。这一时期的植物学论著承认这些知识交流的核心地位。然而，随着欧洲势力在世界各地的增长，欧洲植物学家越来越把自己想象为直接与植物——以及科学的普遍性——交流，无需非欧洲知识的中介。使这门科学成为可能的合作恰恰被掩盖了，植物被要求作为自然元素自己说话。在系统学（分类的科学）史中，普遍前提与合作确立的事实互相隐藏了对方的工作。鉴于它在确立自然中的重要性，这个故事的更多细节值得展开。

Let me return to the moment when plant classification became a site of intellectual discussion throughout Europe—the second half of the sixteenth century. World travelers brought news of unknown and exotic plants from foreign lands. European herbalists were overwhelmed. ‘Thus arose an exciting reconsideration of knowledge, which lasted for two centuries. During this period, plant classification was at the forefront of the development of science. Scholars of the diversity of life worked particularly from two resources: classical treatises, especially the work of Aristotle, and Christian teachings about the workings of God. Both taught of a universal Nature, accessible through reason and by studying life-forms; both suggested the possibility of a singular global system uniting all life. Scholars debated about which was more important: the logical, rational system through which diversity could be charted, or the empirical study of organisms, through which the system could be inductively built. Andrea Cesalpino, a professor at Pisa and papal physician, is known for his early attempt at a universal taxonomy of plants. He relied on Aristotle, as well as his Catholic faith, to construct a rational system to account for diversity. He also developed a dichotomous key to identify plants: On the one hand, it depends on the logic of dichotomy; on the other, it follows the identifying characteristics of real plants, rather than exhausting logical possibilities (Atran 1990: 157). Not much later, Gaspard Bauhin, a Huguenot who presided over the botanical garden at Basel, sought a system of classification through tracing relationships of thousands of plants from around the world (Drayton 2000: 16). Cesalpino has been criticized for being too much of a rationalist; Bauhin has been criticized for not having enough of a logical system. But the concerns about creating a system to understand empirical diversity are clear in each.

让我回到植物分类学成为全欧洲知识讨论场所的时刻——16世纪下半叶。世界旅行者从外国土地带回未知异域植物的消息。欧洲草药学家应接不暇。于是出现了对知识的令人兴奋的重新审视，持续了两个世纪。在此期间，植物分类学处于科学发展的前沿。研究生命多样性的学者特别依赖两种资源：古典论著，尤其是亚里士多德的作品，以及关于上帝运作的基督教教义。两者都教导一种普遍的自然，可通过理性和研究生命形式而接近；两者都暗示一个联合所有生命的单一全球系统的可能性。学者们辩论哪个更重要：可以用来绘制多样性的逻辑理性系统，还是可以借以归纳地构建系统的对生物体的经验研究。比萨教授、教皇御医安德烈亚·切萨尔皮诺以其对植物普遍分类的早期尝试而闻名。他依靠亚里士多德以及他的天主教信仰，构建一个解释多样性的理性系统。他还开发了一种鉴别植物的二分检索表：一方面，它依赖二分法的逻辑；另一方面，它遵循真实植物的识别特征，而不是穷尽逻辑可能性（Atran 1990: 157）。不久之后，主持巴塞尔植物园的胡格诺派加斯帕尔·博安，试图通过追溯来自世界各地数千种植物的关系来建立分类系统（Drayton 2000: 16）。切萨尔皮诺被批评过于理性主义；博安被批评缺乏足够的逻辑系统。但创建系统以理解经验多样性的关切在两人身上都很明显。

Basic to this discussion was the search for universal order, that is, God’s order. Cesalpino, for example, classified plants by the organization of their flower and seed parts, not, as modern biologists might, because of the role of these organs in reproductive biology, but rather because he thought these parts were the best exemplification of God’s plan (Atran 1990: 152). It turned out that classification through flower and seed worked very well to order global plant diversity; it is because of the effectiveness of this framework that botany was so significant as an emergent science. (Zoology, in comparison, was a mess at the time.) Classification by flower and seed showed the potential of systematization.

这场讨论的基础是寻找普遍秩序，即上帝秩序。例如，切萨尔皮诺按花与种子部位的组成来分类植物，不是因为现代生物学家可能认为的这些器官在生殖生物学中的作用，而是因为他认为这些部位最好地体现了上帝的计划（Atran 1990: 152）。结果，按花和种子分类非常有效地整理了全球植物多样性；正是因为这一框架的有效性，植物学作为一门新兴科学才如此重要。（相比之下，当时的动物学一团糟。）按花和种子分类显示了系统化的潜力。

God could be known through reason or through observation, but there was no question about the underlying divine plan that would be revealed. Catholics and Protestants had their differences, but both read the world as God’s book. Among botanists, differences between those who stressed reason versus empirical study were expressed in arguments about the relative priority of the “genus”—a classificatory category that grouped closely related types of plants—versus the “species”—the basic plant type. But arguments for each depended on the stability of God's plan. He created the species, and told humans to name them. He created the logic of genus, which allowed species to develop, each to its proper place. “The Creator of all things, who gave us the faculty for giving names to plants, places in the plants themselves signifying marks” (Tourefort 1719: 54, quoted in Atran 1990: 166).

上帝可以通过理性或观察被认识，但将要揭示的潜在神圣计划是毫无疑问的。天主教徒和新教徒有分歧，但两者都把世界读作上帝的书。在植物学家中，强调理性与强调经验研究的人之间的分歧，表现在关于“属”（一个把密切相关的植物类型归为一类的分类范畴）与“种”（基本植物类型）相对优先级的争论中。但对两者的论证都依赖上帝计划的稳定性。他创造了种，并让人类为它们命名。他创造了属的逻辑，使种得以发展，各归其位。“万物的创造者赋予我们为植物命名的能力，在植物自身中放置了指示性的标记”（Tourefort 1719: 54，引自 Atran 1990: 166）。

This search for the universal—in marks on the plants themselves, and in underlying logics of plant relationships—drew attention away from the knowledge about plants that was learned in dialogue between Europeans and non-Europeans. It might have been possible for Europeans to learn about plants merely by stumbling upon them, but, in fact, they took the easier route of learning about them from other people.
这种对普遍性的寻找——在植物自身的标记中，以及在植物关系的潜在逻辑中——把注意力从欧洲人与非欧洲人对话中学到的植物知识上引开。欧洲人本来也可能只是偶然撞见植物而了解它们，但实际上，他们选择了更容易的途径：向其他人学习。

Historian Richard Grove has described two books about plants in India that drew explicitly from such interactions. Garcia de Orta, a Portuguese doctor in Goa, wrote a treatise on botany in 1563; it was quickly translated into Latin and incorporated into European natural history. The treatise is written as a dialogue between Orta, speaking for the importance of the indigenous knowledge of Goa, and a skeptical interlocutor. Grove writes: “In general the text is remarkably subversive and even hostile to European and Arabic knowledge, regarding it as superfluous in the face of the wealth of accurate local knowledge” (1995: 81). European knowledge was not globally dominant at this period. “Far from imposing European systems of classification and perception on South Asia, the invention of printing and the collation of regional botanical knowledge actually provided an opportunity for the diffusion of indigenous South Asian methodologies of classification throughout the European world, rather than the reverse” (Grove 1995: 80). When the Dutch botanist Hendrik van Reede tot Drakenstein made a new compilation of useful plants of Malabar a century later, he assumed a similar respect for indigenous knowledge. His botanical illustrations were annotated in five languages, including the local Malayam, Arabic, and Latin (Drayton 2000: Plate 3). His text discusses his special reliance on Ezhava collectors of the “toddy-tapper” caste, who were adept at medical knowledge as well as identification of plants. His classifications, which feature Ezhava knowledge, were readily absorbed into European discussions.

历史学家理查德·格罗夫描述了两本关于印度植物的书，它们明确取材于这类互动。果阿的葡萄牙医生加西亚·德·奥尔塔于1563年写了一部植物学论著；它很快被译成拉丁文，并入欧洲自然史。该论著以对话形式写成，奥尔塔代表果阿本土知识的重要性，一位怀疑的对话者与之辩论。格罗夫写道：“总体而言，文本对欧洲和阿拉伯知识具有非凡的颠覆性，甚至敌意，认为在丰富的准确地方知识面前，这些知识是多余的”（1995: 81）。在这一时期，欧洲知识并未在全球占主导地位。“远非把欧洲的分类与感知系统强加于南亚，印刷术的发明和区域植物学知识的整理，实际上为南亚本土分类方法在整个欧洲世界的传播提供了机会，而不是相反”（Grove 1995: 80）。一个世纪后，荷兰植物学家亨德里克·范·里德·托特·德拉肯斯坦编纂马拉巴尔有用植物的新汇编时，也表现出对本土知识的类似尊重。他的植物插图用五种语言注释，包括当地马拉雅拉姆语、阿拉伯语和拉丁语（Drayton 2000: Plate 3）。他的文本讨论了他对“棕榈汁采集者”（toddy-tapper）种姓的埃扎瓦采集者的特别依赖，这些人既精通医学知识，也擅长识别植物。他的分类突出埃扎瓦知识，这些分类很容易被欧洲讨论吸收。

Yet discussions among Europeans refused to acknowledge this global sharing of knowledge. Instead, they focused on the formation of a universal system of classification. John Ray, known for his “grammar” of botany (Atran 1990: 61), obviously read van Reede: “Who could believe that in one province of Malabar, hardly a vast place, there could be three hundred unique, indigenous species of trees and fruit?” (Ray 1686: sig. A3v quoted in Drayton 2000: 18). Yet he attributed no importance to the Ezhava dialogue that brought those species to him. The system itself was knowledge, not its component parts.

然而，欧洲人之间的讨论拒绝承认这种全球知识共享。相反，他们专注于形成普遍的分类系统。以植物“语法”闻名的约翰·雷（Atran 1990: 61）显然读过范·里德：“谁能相信，在马拉巴尔的一个省，几乎不算一个广阔地方，竟有三百种独特的本土树木和水果？”（Ray 1686: sig. A3v，引自 Drayton 2000: 18）。但他并不重视把这些物种带给他的埃扎瓦对话。系统本身就是知识，而不是它的组成部分。
Carl Linnaeus, known as the father of modern biological classification, explained the importance of the system in unifying and ordering a singular global knowledge:
被称为现代生物分类学之父的卡尔·林奈，解释了系统在统一和整理单一全球知识方面的重要性：

The system is for botany the thread of Ariadna, without which there is chaos. Let us take, for example, an unknown plant of the Indies, and let a botanophile leaf through descriptions, figures, every index; he will not find it unless by chance. But a systematist will determine it straight away, be it old or new. ... The system indicates the plants, even those it does not mention; this, the enumeration of a catalog can never do. (Linnaeus 1751: sec. 156, quoted in Atran 1990: 170–71)
系统是植物学的阿里阿德涅之线，没有它，只有混沌。让我们以一株未知的印度诸地（the Indies）的植物为例，让一位植物爱好者翻阅描述、插图、每一个索引；除非碰巧，他不会找到它。但系统学家会立刻鉴定它，无论新旧。……系统指示植物，甚至包括它没有提到的植物；这是目录的列举永远做不到的。（Linnaeus 1751: sec. 156，引自 Atran 1990: 170–71）

The system takes precedence over the plant, as well as the process through which that plant was gathered “out there.” Linneaus unselfconsciously adopted van Reede’s Malabar classifications without noting them as foreign (Grove 1995: 90). For him, all correct knowledge could be united through the use of a universal method. The method is the key to Nature. “Nowhere has the Supreme Creator exposed as many objects to the senses of man as in the Plant Realm, which covers and fills the globe we inhabit. Thus, if there be anywhere a proper method, it is that whereby we may hope to obtain a clear idea of Plants” (Linneaus 1737, quoted in Atran 1990: 151). Since it uncovers the handiwork of God, the system of classification must form a unified, homogeneous whole. There is no understanding here of knowledge as gained in dialogue—and certainly not dialogue between Christians and non-Christians.

系统优先于植物，也优先于那株植物“在那里”被采集的过程。林奈不自觉地采用了范·里德的马拉巴尔分类，却没有注明它们是外来的（Grove 1995: 90）。对他来说，所有正确的知识都可以通过使用一种普遍方法联合起来。方法是通往自然的钥匙。“至高创造者从未像在植物界那样，把如此多的对象暴露给人的感官，植物界覆盖并充满我们居住的地球。因此，如果任何地方有恰当的方法，那就是我们借以有望获得植物清晰概念的方法”（Linnaeus 1737，引自 Atran 1990: 151）。由于它揭示上帝的杰作，分类系统必须构成一个统一、同质的整体。这里没有把知识理解为在对话中获得的理解——当然也不是基督徒与非基督徒之间的对话。

As European hegemony grew, European knowledge increasingly directed global programs. If botanists came to see themselves as alone with Nature, it was because of this political power as well as the insight of “the system” in which all knowledges could be absorbed. Scholars of colonialism have pointed to the texts of eighteenthand nineteenth-century European botanists, gathering plants in non-European locales, as models for imperial consciousness. In contrast to the earlier period, European botanists wrote of the plants but not the people. Their texts emptied the landscapes they studied of human inhabitants, making them appropriate for European settlement and conquest (Pratt 1992; Carter 1987). In the process, they suppressed attention to the practices in which at least some of their knowledge was gained.

随着欧洲霸权增长，欧洲知识越来越主导全球纲领。如果植物学家逐渐把自己看作与自然独处，那既是因为这种政治权力，也是因为“系统”的洞见——所有知识都可以被吸收其中。殖民主义学者指出，18、19世纪欧洲植物学家在非欧洲地点采集植物的文本，是帝国意识的典范。与更早时期相比，欧洲植物学家写植物，却不写人。他们的文本清空了所研究地景中的人类居民，使其适合欧洲定居与征服（Pratt 1992; Carter 1987）。在此过程中，他们压抑了对至少部分知识借以获得的那种实践的关注。

Contemporary efforts to describe plants around the world continue to rely on this emptying out of Nature: Although they often depend on folk experts familiar with local flora, they disavow collaboration except among scientists. Celia Lowe (1999) has studied the species-collection activities of a conservation organization in the Indonesian Togean Islands. She found that English-speaking foreign volunteers objected to learning native names; they imagined their task in finding Nature to be the direct matching of organisms and internationally recorded Latin species names. Their Indonesian hosts and guides juggled local, national, English, and Latin species names, and they used their familiarity with multiple systems to identify species. But they, too, favored Latin names to show their affinities with international science; in their reports, only Latin names counted. This use and disavowal of cross-cultural collaboration also characterizes commercial bioprospecting. In her study of pharmaceutical bioprospecting in Mexico, Corinne Hayden (2003) found that researchers depended upon folk knowledge of plants to acquire biologically active samples. The researchers she studied bought plants from market vendors, who described for them herbs used within Mexican folk medicine. However, it was protocol that samples forwarded to their North American partners for further testing be divested of this folk medical information. To count as scientific samples, the biological material was purified from the history of its discovery.

当代描述世界各地植物的努力继续依赖这种对自然的清空：尽管它们常常依靠熟悉当地植物的民间专家，却否认除科学家之间的合作之外的任何合作。西莉亚·洛（1999）研究了印尼托吉安群岛一个保护组织的物种采集活动。她发现，讲英语的外国志愿者反对学习当地名称；他们把自己的任务想象为直接把生物体与国际记录的拉丁物种名匹配。他们的印尼东道主和向导则在地方、国家、英语和拉丁物种名之间周旋，利用自己对多个系统的熟悉来识别物种。但他们也偏爱拉丁名，以显示自己与国际科学的亲近；在他们的报告中，只有拉丁名算数。这种对跨文化合作的使用与否认也表征了商业生物勘探。科琳·海登（2003）对墨西哥制药生物勘探的研究发现，研究人员依赖植物的民间知识来获得具有生物活性的样本。她研究的研究人员从市场商贩那里购买植物，商贩向他们描述墨西哥民间医学中使用的草药。然而，规程要求，转交给其北美合作伙伴进一步测试的样本必须剥离这些民间医学信息。为了算作科学样本，生物材料被从其发现史中净化出来。

This is a very specific Nature. As the touchstone of biodiversity discourse, it is a resource for environmental politics, and it is one way of encompassing the local within the globe. It also can be criticized for its imperial gaze. Might it be possible to attend to Nature’s collaborative origins without losing the advantages of its global reach?
这是一种非常特定的自然。作为生物多样性话语的试金石，它是环境政治的资源和一种把地方纳入全球的方式；也可以因其帝国式凝视而受到批评。能否既关注自然的合作起源，又不失去其全球触及的优势？
Meanwhile, there are other possibilities for uniting God and Nature. I turn to a different way to the universal, and to the local in the global.
与此同时，还有把上帝与自然结合的其他可能性。我转向通往普遍、以及通往全球中之地方的另一种方式。
自然被定位——在一种全球凝视中

[W]hen we contemplate the whole globe as one great dewdrop, striped and dotted with continents and islands, flying through space with other stars all singing and shining together as one, the whole universe appears as an infinite storm of beauty.
当我们把整个地球看成一滴巨大的露珠，上面条纹斑驳、点缀着大陆和岛屿，与群星一起在太空中飞行，所有星辰一同歌唱、闪耀如一体，整个宇宙便显现为一场无限的美的风暴。
——约翰·缪尔，《阿拉斯加游记》（Travels in Alaska）

Nature soared in Europe and North America in the second half of the nineteenth century—in the gaze of educated travelers, in amateur and professional natural history, in emergent natural sciences, in philosophy, and in poetry. Looking back at this period, contemporary environmentalists single out Scottish-American nature writer John Muir as a prophet of Nature. Muir was a master of rhetoric who conjured reverence for Nature and zeal in protecting its significant wild places. In these wild places, he argued, the global force of Nature is condensed and made available in all its beauty and power for the appreciation of the cosmopolitan pilgrim.
19世纪下半叶，自然在欧洲和北美翱翔——在受过教育的旅行者的凝视中，在业余和专业自然史中，在新兴自然科学中，在哲学和诗歌中。回望这一时期，当代环保主义者把苏格兰裔美国自然作家约翰·缪尔视为自然的先知。缪尔是一位修辞大师，他召唤对自然的敬畏，以及保护其重要荒野地方的热情。他主张，在这些荒野地方，自然的全球力量被凝缩，以其全部美丽与力量提供给世界主义朝圣者欣赏。

This vision of a condensed and located global Nature moved a public, who, like Muir, imagined themselves as travelers in a wide and astonishing world. Muir’s rhetoric galvanized an emergent movement of nature appreciators, bringing together natural scientists and lay people to create a new kind of public advocacy. Together with businessmen who promoted tourism and patriots who imagined U.S. wilderness as an equivalent to European monuments, these nature appreciators invented the idea of national parks, an idea that proved charismatic enough to spread around the world. The national park idea catered to a model of citizenship that privileged those who imagined themselves as cosmopolitan and civilized travelers, and thus potential park visitors. Wild nature would teach and refresh the cosmopolitan heart. Without a coalition of public forces, this vision would never have flourished. Yet its focus on personal inspiration in the encounter between an individual and Nature denied all social mediation.

这种凝缩且定位的全球自然观，打动了那些像缪尔一样把自己想象为广阔而惊人的世界中的旅行者的公众。缪尔的修辞激发了新兴的自然欣赏者运动，把自然科学家和普通人联合起来，创造了一种新的公共倡导。与推广旅游的商人以及把美国荒野想象为欧洲纪念碑对等物的爱国者一起，这些自然欣赏者发明了国家公园的理念，这一理念被证明具有足够的感召力，传播到全世界。国家公园理念迎合了一种公民身份模式，它赋予那些把自己想象为世界主义、文明旅行者的人以特权，因此他们也是潜在的公园游客。荒野自然会教导并滋养世界主义者的心灵。如果没有公共力量的联盟，这一愿景永远不会繁荣。然而，它专注于个人与自然相遇时的个人灵感，否认了一切社会中介。

As in my previous example, the collaborative construction of Natural facts—here including inspiration—was shrouded by an axiom of unity in which individual experiences and observations could be referred directly to the universal. Here, too, the axiom of unity depended on the interplay of Nature and God. Yet Muir’s God was personal and pantheistic, leading him to discover not the system behind all diversity but rather the totality in the local, the global at home. The collaborations on which it depended (and which it hid) did not cross oceans but instead forged a cosmopolitanism ready to rebuild the nation. This coalescence, with its wide-reaching effects on global nature loving (see chapter 4), is worth exploring in more depth.

如同我之前的例子，自然事实——这里包括灵感——的合作建构被一条统一性公理所遮蔽，个别经验和观察可以直接被归结为普遍。同样，这条统一性公理依赖自然与上帝的相互作用。然而缪尔的上帝是人格化的、泛神论的，这使他发现的不是所有多样性背后的系统，而是地方中的总体性，在家的全球。它所依赖的（并隐藏的）合作并没有跨越海洋，而是锻造了一种准备重建国家的世界主义。这种聚合，及其对全球自然之爱的广泛影响（见第四章），值得更深入地探讨。

John Muir grew up with a potent mixture of Nature and God. His father was a strict and zealous Christian who, in pursuit of religious mission, moved the family from Scotland to rural Wisconsin. Muir recalls his childhood there as full of discipline and pioneer challenges. As a young man, Muir spent some time at the University of Wisconsin, where he was introduced to transcendentalist philosophy and botany. Evading the draft, he spent two years in search of rare plants in Canada. He returned to the United States to work in a factory in Indianapolis, where an industrial accident blinded him temporarily. In his recollections, Muir credits the accident for turning his path more fully toward Nature—as God. “I bade adieu to all my mechanical inventions, determined to devote the rest of my life to the study of the inventions of God” (Lankford 1991: 46).

约翰·缪尔在自然与上帝的强烈混合中长大。他的父亲是一位严格而狂热的基督徒，为了追求宗教使命，把家从苏格兰搬到威斯康星乡村。缪尔回忆那里的童年充满纪律与拓荒挑战。年轻时，缪尔在威斯康星大学待了一段时间，在那里接触到超验主义哲学和植物学。为逃避征兵，他在加拿大寻找稀有植物两年。他回到美国，在印第安纳波利斯的一家工厂工作，一次工业事故使他暂时失明。在回忆中，缪尔把这次事故归功于让他的道路更彻底地转向自然——作为上帝。“我告别了我所有的机械发明，决心把余生献给研究上帝的发明”（Lankford 1991: 46）。

In 1867, at the age of 29, Muir traveled south, determined to see the grandeur of Nature in South America as described by world explorer Alexander Humboldt. “How intensely I desire to be Humboldt!” he wrote to a friend (Fox 1981: 47). But a bout of malaria in Florida convinced him to travel west instead of south. He took a boat to California and walked east toward the Sierra Nevada Mountains. When he recalled his first glimpse of the Sierras later, it was with that potent religious vision of Nature that characterized so much of his writing. Starting from the western mountains, he looked east over California’s Central Valley, which at that time was strewn with flowers. “And from the eastern boundary of this vast golden flower-bed rose the mighty Sierra, miles in height, and so gloriously colored and so radiant, it seemed not clothed with light, but wholly composed of it, like the wall of some celestial city” (Muir 1988: 2). He was even more deeply moved upon finding himself in the spectacular Yosemite Valley. “I feel like preaching these mountains like an apostle,” he wrote (Fox 1981: 12). Although he later settled in San Francisco, and, after his marriage, on a ranch outside Oakland, it was Yosemite that remained the center of his gaze.

1867年，29岁的缪尔向南旅行，决心去看世界探险家亚历山大·洪堡所描述的南美洲自然的壮丽。“我是多么强烈地渴望成为洪堡！”他在给朋友的信中写道（Fox 1981: 47）。但在佛罗里达的一次疟疾发作说服他向西而不是向南。他乘船到加利福尼亚，向东步行前往内华达山脉。后来回忆起第一次瞥见内华达山脉时，他带着那种强烈的宗教性自然观，这成为他许多写作的特征。从西部山脉出发，他向东眺望加利福尼亚中央谷地，当时那里遍布鲜花。“从这片广阔金色花床的东部边界，升起雄伟的内华达山脉，高耸数英里，色彩如此辉煌、光芒如此四射，它似乎不是披着光，而是完全由光构成，像某座天城的城墙”（Muir 1988: 2）。当他发现自己置身壮观的约塞米蒂谷时，他更为深深感动。“我觉得自己要像使徒一样宣讲这些山脉，”他写道（Fox 1981: 12）。虽然他后来定居旧金山，婚后住在奥克兰郊外的一个牧场，但约塞米蒂始终是他凝视的中心。

Muir’s descriptions of Yosemite helped others see Nature’s power. Some of these were men of influence: philosopher Ralph Waldo Emerson; future president Theodore Roosevelt. Others were friends and colleagues. Muir cofounded the Sierra Club, bringing together nature lovers, scientists, and advocates for the preservation of nature, and thus crystallizing that amateurprofessional-activist synthesis that still invigorates environmentalism today. Meanwhile, Muir’s writing mobilized an American love of Nature. One result of this mobilization was legislation designed to protect Yosemite Valley—passed first by California and then by the federal government to designate it a national park. Muir, then, is credited with inspiring the national parks movement that spread in and beyond the United States.

缪尔对约塞米蒂的描述帮助他人看到自然的力量。其中一些人是有影响力的人物：哲学家拉尔夫·沃尔多·爱默生；未来的总统西奥多·罗斯福。其他人是朋友和同事。缪尔共同创立了塞拉俱乐部，把自然爱好者、科学家和保护自然的倡导者联合起来，从而结晶了那种业余者—专业人士—活动家的综合，它至今仍为环保主义注入活力。与此同时，缪尔的写作动员了美国人对自然的热爱。这种动员的一个结果是旨在保护约塞米蒂谷的立法——先由加州通过，然后由联邦政府指定为国家公园。因此，缪尔被认为启发了在美国内外传播的国家公园运动。

Muir’s message depended on dramatic, emotionally charged modes of expression, infused with religious rhetoric. Consider Muir’s famous indictment of those who would dam Yosemite’s Hetch Hetchy Valley for a water reservoir: “The temple destroyers, devotees of raging commercialism, seem to have a perfect contempt for Nature, and, instead of lifting their eyes to the God of the mountains, lift them to the Almighty Dollar. Dam Hetch Hetchy! As well dam for water-tanks the people’s cathedrals and churches, for no holier temple has ever been consecrated by the heart of man” (Smith 1987: 177). This passage is characteristic of Muir’s identification of Nature as a focus of religious devotion. It mobilizes an advocacy for the sacred, and for the locally sacred—our church—as well as the universal religion it represents. Nature is God, in Hetch Hetchy and beyond. Muir was a priest of Nature, bringing it devotees. On meeting Emerson, Muir wrote: “I invite you to join me in a month’s worship with Nature in the high temples of the great Sierra Crown beyond our holy Yosemite.... With most cordial regards I am yours in Nature, John Muir” (Fox 1981: 5). Scholars of Muir have noted that Muir’s identification of God and Nature is hardly Christian orthodoxy.

However, Muir’s worship of Nature shares much with the heterodox Protestant Christianity he knew best. Nature, like God, forms the basis of a universal Truth, accessible through direct experience and study. To study a particular instance offers a window into the universal. The local enfolds into the global and the universal; our devotions must simultaneously know the local and its transcendence.

缪尔的讯息依赖戏剧性、充满情感的表达方式，浸透着宗教修辞。想想缪尔对那些要筑坝拦截约塞米蒂赫奇赫奇谷作水库的人的著名控诉：“神庙破坏者、狂热商业主义的信徒，似乎对自然怀有完全的蔑视，他们不抬眼看山中之神，而是抬眼看万能的美元。给赫奇赫奇筑坝吧！不如也为人民的座堂和教堂筑坝作水箱，因为人心从未奉献过比这更神圣的神殿”（Smith 1987: 177）。这段话典型地体现了缪尔把自然认同为宗教虔诚的焦点。它动员了对神圣者、对地方神圣者——我们的教堂——的倡导，也倡导它所代表的普遍宗教。自然是上帝，在赫奇赫奇，也在别处。缪尔是自然的祭司，为它带来信徒。在见到爱默生时，缪尔写道：“我邀请您与我一起，在我们神圣的约塞米蒂之外伟大的塞拉皇冠的高山神殿中，与自然共度一个月的礼拜……致以最诚挚的问候，在自然中忠于您的，约翰·缪尔”（Fox 1981: 5）。缪尔研究者注意到，缪尔把上帝与自然等同起来，很难说是基督教正统。
然而，缪尔对自然的崇拜与他最熟悉的异端新教基督教有许多共同之处。自然和上帝一样，构成普遍真理的基础，可通过直接经验与研究接近。研究一个特殊实例，就打开一扇通往普遍的窗户。地方包蕴于全球与普遍之中；我们的虔诚必须同时认识地方及其超越。

Muir worked back and forth between evoking global Nature and its local instances. One interpreter of his writing speaks of the ubiquity of “planetary passages,” in which references to the “earth-planet” offer a heightened emotional charge to landscape descriptions (Lankford 1991: 35).
Yosemite thus instantiated global space and time.
缪尔在召唤全球自然与其地方实例之间来回工作。他写作的一位解释者谈到“行星段落”的普遍存在，其中对“地球—行星”的提及为地景描述增添了更高的情感强度（Lankford 1991: 35）。
约塞米蒂由此实例化了全球的空间与时间。

Yosemite temples will be the more enjoyed by those who have traced ... the crystallization of the granite in the dark, thousands of centuries before development, and who know how in the fullness of time the sun called to lift water out of the sea in vapor which was carried by the winds to the mountains, crystallized into snow among the clouds, to fall on the summits, form glaciers, and bring Yosemite Valley ... to light. (Muir quoted in Lankford 1991: 41)
那些追溯过……花岗岩在黑暗中的结晶过程——在其发育之前数千个世纪——并且知道时机成熟时，太阳如何召唤海水化作蒸汽升起，蒸汽被风带到山间，在云中结晶为雪，降落在峰顶，形成冰川，把约塞米蒂谷……带入光明的人，会更加欣赏约塞米蒂的神庙。（缪尔，引自 Lankford 1991: 41）

Muir’s Nature—and his Yosemite—are forged in a scale-making project in which the local and the global are wrapped together and charged by the principles of the universal. Yosemite stood for the possibility of individual contact, through study and experience, with the hugeness of a global and universal Nature. Not any individual, however, can achieve this gaze. The subject who can grasp Nature here is the cosmopolitan traveler. Muir’s use of travel writing as the genre in which he conveyed his sense of Nature’s wonders is not incidental. Like Humboldt who inspired him, Muir appeals to the free metropolitan intellect who can imagine him- or herself in global travel. It is tempting to identify this reader as white, male, and wealthy, but this is not historically accurate. White women were among the most enthusiastic audiences for Muir’s writing, and women’s clubs energized the movement to create parks and nature reserves (Smith 1987).

Moreover, Muir projected an ambiguous or androgynous gender identification in his writing, drawing female readers and gentle men (Jespersen 1997). Indeed, Muir’s opponents weakened him by portraying his cause as feminine; some scholars have argued that this feminization of nature protection kept environmentalism at a low profile through the first half of the twentieth century (Smith 1987). Race and class are also ambiguously implicated. Rather than reduce him to a “type,” it is useful to look at who joined this collaborative momentum.

缪尔的自然——以及他的约塞米蒂——在一个尺度制造项目中被锻造，其中地方与全球被包裹在一起，并被普遍原则赋予力量。约塞米蒂代表了一种可能性：通过研究与经验，个人可以与一个全球性、普遍性自然的庞大整体接触。然而，并非任何个人都能获得这种凝视。在这里能够把握自然的主体是世界主义旅行者。缪尔使用旅行写作这一体裁来传达他对自然奇观的感受，并非偶然。像启发他的洪堡一样，缪尔诉诸自由的大都市知识分子，他们能想象自己置身全球旅行。人们很容易把这位读者认定为白人、男性、富有，但这在历史上并不准确。白人女性是缪尔写作最热情的受众之一，妇女俱乐部为创建公园和自然保护区的运动注入了活力（Smith 1987）。
此外，缪尔在写作中投射出一种模糊的或兼具两性特征的性别认同，吸引了女性读者和文雅的男性（Jespersen 1997）。事实上，缪尔的对手通过把他的事业描绘为女性化来削弱他；一些学者认为，这种对自然保护的女性化使环保主义在20世纪上半叶未能获得广泛关注（Smith 1987）。种族和阶级也以模糊的方式牵涉其中。与其把他简化为一个“类型”，不如看看谁加入了这一合作势头。

Consider, then, Muir’s most powerful allies: scientists, nature lovers, and a certain set of entrepreneurs and politicians. Each of these was invested in the cosmopolitan gaze upon Nature. In science, Muir’s affinities were with scientists who themselves were working through the relation between local and global instances of universal Natural law. Muir’s study of glaciation in Yosemite Valley was in direct dialogue with Louis Agassiz, a Harvard naturalist who studied the chronology of rock strata as evidence of a global era of glaciation. Muir also worked with evolutionary biologist Asa Gray in collecting Western flora. In studies of glaciation and botany, Muir’s sense that Nature formed a book that could be read—a global/local instancing of the universal—brought him inside an important current of nineteenth-century naturalism.

那么，考虑缪尔最强大的盟友：科学家、自然爱好者，以及某类企业家和政治家。他们每一个人都投入于对自然的世界主义凝视。在科学中，缪尔的亲和力在于那些自身正在处理普遍自然法则的地方与全球实例之间关系的科学家。缪尔对约塞米蒂谷冰川作用的研究，直接与哈佛博物学家路易斯·阿加西对话，后者研究岩层年代学，作为全球冰川期证据。缪尔还与演化生物学家阿萨·格雷合作采集西部植物。在冰川学和植物学研究中，缪尔认为自然构成一本可读的书——普遍性的全球/地方实例化——这把他带入19世纪博物学的重要潮流。

Muir’s most enduring fans have been nature lovers and environmentalists. It is only because of their efforts that his legacy continues to be important today. Even during Muir’s lifetime, they came in different sorts, from the activist hikers of the Sierra Club, to the women’s clubs already mentioned, to tourists, scholars, and publishers. Despite their differences, the Californians among these nature lovers shared certain orientations: California was a new state, still at the edge of being a colonial territory. Through much of the nineteenth century, “science” in California consisted mostly of military surveys, commissioned for the purpose of securing administrative control. Muir formed part of a change in which science and nature loving signaled a more civilian form of citizenship. The settlers became citizens through their love of the land. Muir’s evocation of Nature helped to secure this form of settler consciousness (Smith 1987)

缪尔最持久的粉丝一直是自然爱好者和环保主义者。正是因为他们的努力，他的遗产今天仍然重要。即使在缪尔生前，他们也以不同种类出现，从塞拉俱乐部的参与行动的徒步者，到已经提到的妇女俱乐部，再到游客、学者和出版商。尽管有差异，这些自然爱好者中的加州人共享某些取向：加州是一个新州，仍处于是否属于殖民领地的模糊边界上。19世纪的大部分时间里，加州的“科学”主要由军事勘测构成，委托目的是确保行政控制。缪尔参与了这样一场变化：科学与自然之爱标志着一种更平民化的公民身份形式。定居者通过热爱土地而成为公民。缪尔对自然的召唤帮助确立了这种定居者意识（Smith 1987）。

The support of these groups only translated into political effectiveness, however, because of influential allies: the bosses of the Southern Pacific Railroad. Muir formed a friendship with railroad baron E. H. Harriman, who convinced the U.S. Congress to designate Yosemite a national park (Fox 1981). The railroad was interested in the development of tourism since tourists came to the western United States mainly by train. Larger issues of what it meant to be a citizen were also at stake. The railroad block promoted notions of citizenship in which cosmopolitan travelers—people on the move—were the quintessential U.S. citizens. These people could benefit from encounters with Nature; indeed, these mobile and malleable citizens could be made as such in encounters with Nature. The railroad bosses fought for a particular point of view in the making of the western United States, and Muir’s version of Nature supported their struggle.

然而，这些群体的支持只有通过有影响力的盟友才能转化为政治效力：南太平洋铁路的老板们。缪尔与铁路大亨 E. H. 哈里曼结成友谊，后者说服美国国会把约塞米蒂指定为国家公园（Fox 1981）。铁路对旅游业的发展感兴趣，因为游客主要通过火车来到美国西部。关于作为公民意味着什么的更大问题也牵涉其中。铁路集团推广这样一种公民观念：世界主义旅行者——移动中的人——是典型美国公民。这些人可以从与自然的相遇中受益；事实上，这些流动而可塑的公民可以在与自然的相遇中被塑造成这样的人。铁路老板们在美国西部的制造中为一种特定观点而斗争，缪尔版本的自然支持了他们的斗争。

Muir’s articulation also created opponents and areas of invisibility. Ranchers were Muir’s most explicit enemies; ranchers used the wilderness rather than experiencing or studying it. They were cut off from the universal; they destroyed it through inattention. Ranchers became the icon of one side of a dichotomy dividing the exploitation of Nature from its study and protection.
缪尔的接合也制造了对手和不可见的区域。牧场主是缪尔最明确的敌人；牧场主利用荒野，而不是体验或研究它。他们被排除在普遍之外；他们因不注意而毁灭它。牧场主成为二分法一方的象征，这种二分法把对自然的开发与其研究和保护分隔开来。

This dichotomy forms the basis of the most well-known divide in U.S. environmental politics: the divide between “conservation” and “preservation.” (These terms take on particular meanings for this debate; after discussing the debate I return to using the term “conservation” much more broadly.) Histories of U.S. environmentalism often begin with Muir’s disagreements with Gifford Pinchot, who became the first head of the U.S. Forest Service.
这种二分法构成美国环境政治中最著名的分歧的基础：“保育”（conservation）与“保存”（preservation）之间的分歧。（这些术语在这场辩论中具有特定含义；讨论完这场辩论后，我将回到更广泛地使用“保育”一词。）美国环保主义的历史常常从缪尔与吉福德·平肖的分歧开始，平肖成为美国林务局的第一任局长。

Pinchot, educated in the emerging European science of scientific forestry, believed that forests should serve economic and state-administrative interests. Ranching, timbering, and other forms of commercial use were a proper part of forest management; the goal of forestry was to maintain a national stock of forest lands precisely for such uses. Pinchot here stands for a view of the forests that combines utilitarian use and bureaucratic control, in this story called “conservation.” Muir, in contrast, stands for the full protection of Nature for its own sake.
平肖接受过新兴欧洲科学林业的教育，认为森林应服务于经济和国家行政利益。牧牛、伐木和其他形式的商业利用是森林管理的正当部分；林业的目标正是为国家维持森林土地储备以供这些用途。平肖在这里代表一种结合功利性使用与官僚控制的森林观，在这个故事中称为“保育”。相比之下，缪尔代表为了自然本身而全面保护自然。

Both sides of this debate formed their momentum through culturally specific claims about the universal that blocked attention to the sometimes discordant collaborations that enlivened each agenda. Scientific forestry promoted universals of rationalism and profit. The uses of nature could be planned through a calculus of management. This agenda drew bureaucrats and businessmen. It also appealed to popular democracy: people should use forests. In this spirit, small as well as large users have been drawn to the resource management agenda. However, it is useful to remember that the legacies of both Pinchot and Muir articulate problematic universals and draw dangerous allies into the struggle for environmental well-being.
这场辩论双方都通过文化特定的普遍性主张形成势头，这些主张阻挡人们关注使各自议程活跃起来的、有时不协调的合作。科学林业推广理性主义与利润的普遍性。自然的各种用途可以通过管理计算来规划。这一议程吸引了官僚和商人。它也诉诸大众民主：人民应该使用森林。本着这种精神，小用户和大用户都被吸引到资源管理议程中。然而，值得记住的是，平肖和缪尔的遗产都阐发了成问题的普遍性，并把危险的盟友拉进环境福祉的斗争。

The debate reminds us why Muir’s vision continues to inspire. In contrast to the resource managers, Muir tells us that Nature cannot be reduced to the needs of capitalism and the state. Nature deserves protection for itself. Here too are the shortcomings of the collaborative legacy of Muir’s vision. The nature protection that Muir stimulated has not done well in forming alliances with local residents, who tend to be dismissed as users and therefore despoilers of nature. It has been easier to gain the support of distant corporate sponsors, who, like Muir’s railroad friends, support nature tourism, rather than resident communities. As the national park idea spread around the world, parks advocacy formed even more problematic alliances with colonial heritages of resettlement and the displacement of indigenous residents. Residents have been evicted from nature reserves by force; local livelihoods have been disrupted. Recent environmental scholarship is full of documentation on the conflicts between residents and parks.

These alliances and enmities are the collaborative legacy John Muir set into motion. They form the power and the danger of this legacy; they set an awkward agenda. Yet nature lovers rarely acknowledge these issues; certainly Muir himself did not. Why? Muir’s vision of Nature itself shut out the possibility that collaborations were important. Nature was knowable through direct experience. We need no conversations to make Nature come to life; we want direct access to the universal text. “The clearest way into the Universe is through a forest wilderness” (Muir quoted in Lankford 1991: 38). Environmentalists and nature lovers must struggle with this legacy, which offers both the transcendent power of Nature and the inability to know one’s own collaborative positions.

这场辩论提醒我们缪尔的愿景为何继续激励人。与资源管理者相反，缪尔告诉我们，自然不能被简化为资本主义和国家的需要。自然应为其自身而受到保护。这里也有缪尔愿景合作遗产的缺陷。缪尔所激发的自然保护，在与当地居民结盟方面做得不好，当地居民往往被斥为使用者，从而是自然的掠夺者。获得远方企业赞助者的支持更容易，他们像缪尔的铁路朋友一样支持自然旅游，而不是居民社区。随着国家公园理念在世界各地传播，公园倡导与殖民遗产的重新安置和土著居民流离失所形成了更成问题的联盟。居民被武力驱逐出自然保护区；地方生计受到扰乱。晚近的环境学术研究充满了关于居民与公园之间冲突的记录。

这些联盟与敌意是约翰·缪尔启动的合作遗产。它们构成这份遗产的力量与危险；它们设定一个尴尬的议程。然而自然爱好者很少承认这些问题；缪尔本人当然也没有。为什么？缪尔对自然本身的愿景排除了合作很重要的可能性。自然可以通过直接经验被认识。我们不需要对话来让自然活起来；我们想要直接进入普遍文本。“进入宇宙最清晰的路，是穿过一片森林荒野”（Muir，引自 Lankford 1991: 38）。环保主义者和自然爱好者必须与这份遗产抗争，它既提供了自然的超越力量，也提供了无法认识自身合作位置的无能。

Meanwhile, the United States launched other understandings of the globe. After World War II, U.S. military intelligence research was responsible for new kinds of globalisms, in which a mechanical vision of the relations of the parts to the whole replaces God as the author of universal laws. Cybernetics, systems dynamics, systems ecology, and circulation models were developed from the insight that systems create their own dynamics. Information about the interrelationship of elements within a system can generate knowledge of the whole. In contrast to Muir’s endorsement of the global condensed in the local, these models bypass locality completely, except as an unmarked moment in scaling up and down. The system of flow and feedback takes precedence to any internal point. The global emerges as a node of systematicity. A key example is the model-making at the heart of public and scientific discussion of global climate change. My focus here is not the making of a universal logic but rather its use in the construction of a new kind of global scale. Collaborations across difference are both demanded and denied in this process.

与此同时，美国推出了对地球的另一些理解。二战后，美国军事情报研究促成了新型全球主义，其中一种关于部分与整体关系的机械论视角取代上帝，成为普遍法则的作者。控制论、系统动力学、系统生态学和环流模型的发展，源于系统创造自身动态的洞见。关于系统内各要素相互关系的信息可以产生关于整体的知识。与缪尔赞成的全球凝缩于地方相反，这些模型完全绕过地方性，除非把它当作尺度放大和缩小中一个未被标记的时刻。流动与反馈的系统优先于任何内部点。全球作为系统性的节点出现。一个关键例子是处于全球气候变化公共与科学讨论核心的模型制造。我在这里关注的不是普遍逻辑的制造，而是它在建构一种新全球尺度中的使用。在这一过程中，跨越差异的合作既被要求，又被否认。

Developing a predictive understanding of global environmental change in order to provide a scientific basis for national and international policy and decision making requires a comprehensive, interdisciplinary approach to studying the total Earth system.
为了给国家和国际政策与决策提供科学基础，发展对全球环境变化的预测性理解，需要一种全面的、跨学科的方法来研究整个地球系统。
—SEDAC, Consortium for International Earth Science Information Network, “a part of NASA’s Earth Observing System Data and Information System,” 1993 brochure
——SEDAC，国际地球科学信息网络联盟，“NASA地球观测系统数据与信息系统的一部分”，1993年宣传册

In the 1990s, global climate change was the center of what environmentalists, and the interested public, thought about when they imagined environmental issues as global. When environmental organizations wanted to prove that they were tapped into transnational networks, they mentioned global climate change. Government officials and businesses pointed to global climate change to index the common problems of the world. One kind of globality, or at least multilocality, of climate change, then, is its multiple referencing by groups in varied social and physical locations.
20世纪90年代，当环保主义者和感兴趣的公众把环境问题想象为全球性时，全球气候变化是他们思考的中心。当环保组织想证明自己接入了跨国网络时，他们就提到全球气候变化。政府官员和商界指出全球气候变化来标示世界的共同问题。因此，气候变化的一种全球性，或至少是多地方性，就是不同社会和自然位置的群体对它的多重指涉。

Climate change seemed “global” to the public, too, because the issue was introduced during a period of concern about transboundary environmental issues: species loss, water pollution, acid rain, radioactivity. In the United States, a hot, dry summer in 1988 corresponded to the peak of public concern about the destruction of the rainforests in Amazonia. The emission of greenhouse gases (carbon dioxide and other gases whose increase in concentration is causing global warming) linked the U.S. climate and the loss of the Brazilian forest. The world was losing the carbon sink of the forests, while the burning of the forests produced more greenhouse gases. The idea of global climate change articulated the new realization that places far apart from each other were still connected for their basic survival, especially through the circulation of air and water.

气候变化在公众看来也显得“全球”，因为这个问题是在人们对跨境环境问题——物种丧失、水污染、酸雨、放射性——关切的时期被引入的。在美国，1988年一个炎热干燥的夏天正好对应公众对亚马孙雨林破坏关切的顶峰。温室气体（二氧化碳和其他浓度增加导致全球变暖的气体）的排放把美国的气候与巴西森林的丧失联系起来。世界正在失去森林的碳汇，而森林燃烧又产生更多温室气体。全球气候变化的想法阐明了新的认识：相隔遥远的地方仍然因基本生存而相互连接，尤其是通过空气和水的循环。

The most easily identified “globality” of this realization, however, has been in the model that climate experts promoted to explain and predict climate change. General Circulation Models (GCM) use the laws of circulation of air and water to generate an abstraction we might call global climate. These models are self-conscious representations. They do not purport to describe the globe but rather to picture it in the model. They simplify and reduce the social and natural world to geophysical laws. In the process, they develop a globe that is unified, neutral, and understandable through the collection and manipulation of information.
然而，这一认识最容易识别的“全球性”出现在气候专家为解释和预测气候变化而推广的模型中。大气环流模型（GCM）运用空气和水的环流定律，生成一种我们可以称为全球气候的抽象。这些模型是自觉的表征。它们并非意在描述地球，而是在模型中描绘它。它们把社会和自然世界简化并还原为地球物理定律。在此过程中，它们通过信息的收集与操作，发展出一个统一、中立、可理解的地球。

This is a specific—even a peculiar—kind of globe. The global scale is privileged above all others. In contrast to Linnean plant classification or Muir-inspired nature appreciation, the global scale is the locus of prediction as well as understanding. Local conditions can be predicted from the global model; that is the point of its globality. Local data may adjust the global model but never defy it. Its globality is all-embracing.
这是一种特定的——甚至奇特的——地球。全球尺度被赋予高于所有其他尺度的特权。与林奈植物分类或缪尔启发的自然欣赏相比，全球尺度既是理解也是预测的所在。地方条件可以从全球模型中被预测；这就是其全球性的要点。地方数据可以调整全球模型，但绝不能违抗它。它的全球性是包罗万象的。

The model declares itself continually to be science. It is expert, neutral, rational, and empirically grounded. We know this, in part, because the model is complex and constantly under revision. It requires the computational prowess of computers because it integrates many factors. It admits to many uncertainties. Because of all the uncertainties integrated into it, using it requires great skill. Experts must train as part of a “community” of model users; they must develop common standards and trust. They should also communicate with the public. Experts use the models to tell the public about risks; public representatives can then debate what to do about these risks. “Uncertainties,” “trust,” “risk”: These terms circle in the model’s orbit. Through them, the model both secures its place as science and stimulates debate. The model unleashes its own dangers: This is its goal. Neither botanists nor nature lovers have used globality to push potential collaborators to the negotiating table, but climate modelers do just that.

模型不断宣称自己是科学。它是专家的、中立的、理性的、以经验为基础的。我们知道这一点，部分是因为模型复杂且不断修订。它需要计算机的计算能力，因为它整合许多因素。它承认许多不确定性。由于其中整合了所有不确定性，使用它需要高超技巧。专家必须在模型使用者“共同体”中接受训练；他们必须发展共同标准与信任。他们还应该与公众沟通。专家用模型告诉公众风险；公众代表随后可以辩论如何应对这些风险。“不确定性”、“信任”、“风险”：这些术语在模型的轨道上循环。通过它们，模型既确保自己作为科学的地位，又激发辩论。模型释放自己的危险：这是它的目标。植物学家和自然爱好者都没有利用全球性把潜在合作者推到谈判桌前，但气候建模者正是这么做的。

, It is my contention that the global commitments of the model are strategic: They are tuned to stimulate international dialogue. They also cover up dialogue through reference to the unified globe of the model. Modelbuilding practitioners are self-conscious about the effects of their models on policy makers and the public. They want to create collaborations, and they know what kind they want. They want their models to show the way to global standards and structures of management. Their models show that only such standards and structures will promote survival. The modelmakers want to bring policy makers into the modeling effort. They want policy makers to be future-oriented global citizens. The model is an attempt to make this happen by denying pre-existing interests and identities—and thus the necessity of negotiation within the collaborations they endorse. The global unit supercedes nations, classes, cultures, or specific business interests. The model’s generalizations promote negotiation by making its necessity disappear into a seamless globe.

我认为模型的全球承诺是战略性的：它们被调校以刺激国际对话。它们也通过指向模型的统一地球来掩盖对话。模型建造实践者自觉关注模型对政策制定者和公众的影响。他们想创造合作，而且知道自己想要哪种合作。他们希望模型为全球标准和管理结构指明道路。他们的模型表明，只有这样的标准和结构才能促进生存。模型制造者想把政策制定者带入建模努力。他们希望政策制定者成为面向未来的全球公民。模型是一种尝试，通过否认既有的利益与身份——从而否认他们所认可的合作中协商的必要性——来实现这一点。全球这一单位超越国家、阶级、文化或特定商业利益。模型的概括促进协商，办法是让协商的必要性消失在一个无缝的地球中。

The models incorporate strategy through the forms of global Nature they delineate. To see this, it is useful to examine the culture of modelers. First impressions, imbued with the shock of cultural difference, can perhaps convey this culture’s strangeness and specificity. I offer an ethnographic arrival story.
模型通过它们描绘的全球自然形式纳入战略。要看到这一点，考察建模者的文化是有用的。第一印象带着文化差异的冲击，也许能传达这种文化的陌生性与特殊性。我提供一个民族志抵达故事。

I had my first taste of global climate models, and their makers, at the “First Open Meeting of the Human Dimensions of Global Environmental Change Community” in 1995 at Duke University in Durham, North Carolina. This was a very specific segment of the “community”: the meeting was organized by political scientists, who have their own global agendas; the modelers present were those most interested in socioeconomic rather than geophysical data. Yet if I ignore the political science and focus on the surprises of my first impressions of modeling, I can introduce some recurrent cultural features.
1995年，在北卡罗来纳州达勒姆的杜克大学，“全球环境变化人文维度共同体第一次公开会议”上，我第一次体验全球气候模型及其制造者。这是“共同体”中一个非常特定的部分：会议由政治学家组织，他们有自己的全球议程；到场的建模者是对社会经济数据而非地球物理数据最感兴趣的那些人。然而，如果我忽略政治学，专注于我对建模第一印象中的惊讶，我就可以介绍一些反复出现的文化特征。

For me, everything seemed exotic: the incessant clicking of laptops in the lecture halls; the parade of computer projections; the use of acronyms; the programmatic nature of much of the research, in which results were just an example of potential. It seemed that U.S. modelers wore dark, drab suits and armed themselves with piles of overheads, while Europeans wore bright jackets and flamboyant ties and spoke of creativity and culture. Women appeared as representatives of official organizations; they hid behind charts. Used to the informality of scholars who imagine themselves as of little public importance, I could tell I had entered an unfamiliar scene of action and effectiveness. Details of dress and presentation were geared for particular policy audiences. More so the models, which, through the ways they surprised me, instructed me in fundamentals.

对我来说，一切似乎都很陌生：演讲厅里笔记本电脑不停的点击声；接连不断的电脑投影演示；缩略词的使用；许多研究的纲领性，其中结果只是潜力的一例。美国建模者似乎穿着深色、单调的西装，带着成堆的幻灯片；欧洲人则穿着鲜艳的夹克和浮夸的领带，谈论创造力和文化。女性作为官方组织的代表出现；她们躲在图表后面。我习惯了那些自认为无足轻重的学者的随和，因此我能看出自己进入了一个陌生的行动与效力场景。衣着和展示的细节是为特定政策受众调校的。模型更是如此，它们通过让我惊讶的方式，教给我基本的东西。

I recall my first surprise: The global scale takes precedence—because it is the scale of the model. A geographer showed us how to use climate models for social science research. We needed to understand the procedures for “downscaling” from the global model to predict local environmental impacts. He used his computer to demonstrate for us how to predict the weather in one Swiss canton two hundred years in the future.
我记得第一个惊讶：全球尺度优先——因为它是模型的尺度。一位地理学家向我们展示如何把气候模型用于社会科学研究。我们需要理解从全球模型“降尺度”以预测地方环境影响的程序。他用电脑向我们演示如何预测瑞士一个州两百年后的天气。

At first, I was just shocked by the temerity of predicting the local from the global. What happened to the social and natural landscape of that canton? Could it mean nothing? Then I did see that his demonstration was not just a direct downscaling. One can “nest” a limited-area atmospheric model within the global climate model, thus including a certain amount of local information. Smaller scale information can be incorporated in global climate models in a number of ways. “Parameters” are introduced into the global model from regional and local empirical studies; these keep the model closer to accepted descriptions of reality. Model users may add data from other sources to create regional and landscape scale predictions. There is considerable interest in “meso-scale” modeling. Finally, there is much discussion among modelers about problems of scale. In a special issue of Science on global environmental problems, for example, two scientists argue that neither “scale-up” nor “scale-down” research paradigms can provide reliable ecological assessments. They advocate “strategic cyclical scaling,” which integrates regional and local empirical data into global models, correcting global projections with the results of smaller-scale monitoring and evaluation of actual effects (Root and Schneider 1995).

起初，我只是震惊于从全球预测地方的胆大妄为。那个州的社会与自然地景怎么了？它可以毫无意义吗？然后我确实看到，他的演示不只是直接降尺度。人们可以在全球气候模型中“嵌套”一个有限区域大气模型，从而纳入一定量的地方信息。较小尺度的信息可以通过多种方式纳入全球气候模型。区域和地方经验研究把“参数”引入全球模型；这些使模型更接近被接受的对现实的描述。模型使用者可以加入其他来源的数据，以创建区域和地景尺度的预测。“中尺度”建模受到相当关注。最后，建模者之间关于尺度问题有许多讨论。例如，在《科学》关于全球环境问题的特刊中，两位科学家论证，“放大”和“缩小”研究范式都不能提供可靠的生态评估。他们提倡“战略性循环缩放”，把区域和地方经验数据整合进全球模型，用较小尺度监测和实际效果评估的结果来校正全球预测（Root and Schneider 1995）。

Within these nuances, a set of assumptions about scale remains. Scales ought to fit neatly inside each other, the small inside the large, each neutral and fully encompassed by the next scale up. If they don’t, we must fiddle, looking for a more realistic fit. The incompatibility of scales is a practical problem. It does not challenge the principles of the model, which requires that the local disappear compatibly inside the global.
在这些细微差别中，一套关于尺度的假设仍然存在。尺度应该整齐地相互嵌套，小的在大的里面，每一个都是中立的，并被上一级尺度完全包含。如果不是，我们必须摆弄，寻找更现实的契合。尺度的不相容是一个实际问题。它并不挑战模型的原则，而模型要求地方以相容的方式消失在全球之中。

My second surprise: Models breed more models. One man lectured on the modeling of uncertainty. It was one of the more unusual kinds of social science I had seen. He discussed, for example, the degree of trust that different climate scientists had in the global climate model, based on a survey. He then correlated their trust with personal characteristics, such as whether they smoked. I thought at first it was a joke, but I hadn’t been around the discussion of uncertainty, or modeling. Models are made more reliable by incorporating uncertainties into the model, that is, by modeling them.
我的第二个惊讶：模型繁殖更多模型。一位男士就不确定性建模作演讲。这是我见过的最不寻常的社会科学之一。例如，他根据一项调查讨论了不同气候科学家对全球气候模型的信任程度。然后他把他们的信任与个人特征相关联，比如是否吸烟。起初我以为这是个玩笑，但我此前没有接触过关于不确定性或建模的讨论。通过把不确定性纳入模型，也就是通过为它们建模，模型变得更加可靠。

Since the emergence of global climate models, much concern has been expressed about the fact that the GCM does not include social information: The world is reduced to physical laws. Modelers have responded by developing more extensive models that incorporate everything. This is called integrated assessment (IA), and it requires combining rather different kinds of models. Social features of the globe are usually modeled using systems dynamics models, which are then combined with geophysical circulation models. Other kinds of modeling may be brought in as well. Since it is not clear how to do this, many forms of integrated assessment compete for attention. Everyone wants to include population and land use, but there are many other categories; some have even tried adding “culture” to that which can be modeled. The common assumption is that everything can be quantified and located as an element of a system of feedback and flow. “Uncertainties” pile up. One IA project admits, “In view of the accumulation of uncertainties, the interpretative and instructive value of the... model is far more important than its predictive capacity, which is limited by the incomplete science upon which it is constructed” (Rotmans 1995b: 3). Is modeling a teaching practice or a predictive science?

自全球气候模型出现以来，人们一直对大气环流模型不包括社会信息这一事实表示关切：世界被还原为物理定律。建模者的回应是开发纳入一切的更广泛模型。这被称为综合评估（IA），它需要结合相当不同的模型。地球的社会特征通常使用系统动力学模型建模，然后与地球物理环流模型结合。其他类型的建模也可能被引入。由于如何做到这一点并不清楚，许多综合评估形式争夺注意力。每个人都想纳入人口和土地利用，但还有许多其他范畴；有些人甚至尝试把“文化”加入可建模之物。共同的假设是，一切都可以被量化并定位为反馈与流动系统的一个要素。“不确定性”堆积起来。一个IA项目承认：“鉴于不确定性的累积，……模型的解释和教育价值远远重要于其预测能力，而预测能力受制于其构建所依据的不完整科学”（Rotmans 1995b: 3）。建模是一种教学实践还是预测科学？

Another surprise: Models must be charismatic and pedagogical. One modeler compared the success of European modeling with the failures of U.S. counterparts. He explained that the first success of climate modeling in Europe occurred as a result of concerns over acid rain. The European Union was just emerging, with transboundary issues as its reason to exist. The modelers brought policy makers from the EU into their modeling efforts. They let them design simulations. The policy makers became involved; they integrated the models into their positions. In contrast, he argued, U.S. modelers have had much less success. Their models are too complex and too academic; policy makers aren’t attracted to them. Modeling, he argued, is a tool, not a declaration of truth.

另一个惊讶：模型必须具有感召力和教育性。一位建模者比较了欧洲建模的成功与美国同行的失败。他解释说，欧洲气候建模的首次成功源于对酸雨的关切。欧盟刚刚兴起，跨境问题是其存在的理由。建模者把欧盟的政策制定者带入建模努力。他们让政策制定者设计模拟。政策制定者参与进来；他们把模型整合进自己的立场。相反，他认为，美国建模者的成功少得多。他们的模型太复杂、太学术；政策制定者不被吸引。他说，建模是一种工具，不是真理的宣告。

The embedding of smaller scales into the global; the enlargement of models to include everything; the policy-driven construction of the models: Together, these features make it possible that models can bring diplomats to the negotiating table. Indeed, the models have helped stimulate negotiations, as in Rio in 1992 and in Kyoto in 1997. Yet, rather than the consensus that modelers hoped for, these negotiations have been arenas of conflict. Two conflicts have dominated the field: differences between representatives of the global north and south, and differences between the United States and Europe. The former takes the unified globe of the models apart, dividing it into sectors with dissimilar interests. The latter disputes environmental science, arguing for other forms of knowledge. Each reveals the collaborative structure of modeling through claims of being excluded.

把较小尺度嵌入全球；扩大模型以包含一切；政策驱动的模型建构：这些特征合在一起，使模型有可能把外交官带到谈判桌前。的确，模型帮助刺激了谈判，如1992年里约和1997年京都。然而，谈判并没有形成建模者希望的共识，反而成了冲突的场域。两种冲突主导了这一领域：全球北方与南方代表之间的差异，以及美国与欧洲之间的差异。前者把模型的统一地球拆开，划分为利益不同的部分。后者质疑环境科学，主张其他形式的知识。每一种冲突都通过被排斥的主张，揭示了建模的合作结构。

Spokespeople for the global south argue that global climate models are an articulation of northern interests. Global climate models show everyone invested in the same reductions of greenhouse gases; they cover up the fact that most of these gases are emitted in northern countries. In blaming southern countries for a share of the greenhouse gas problem, the models also obscure differences between northern and southern emissions. Many greenhouse gases emitted in southern countries are “subsistence emissions,” in contrast to the “luxury emissions” of northern countries. Global modeling, they imply, is not neutral but rather positioned with those wealthy nations who can cut emissions—but want others to help them. In international negotiations before the 1992 Rio Earth Summit, this argument was convincing enough to be incorporated into the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change.

全球南方的发言者主张，全球气候模型是北方利益的接合。全球气候模型表明每个人都投入于同样的温室气体减排；它们掩盖了大部分这些气体在北方国家排放的事实。在把温室气体问题的一部分归咎于南方国家时，模型也模糊了北方与南方排放之间的差异。南方国家排放的许多温室气体是“生存排放”，与北方国家的“奢侈排放”相对。他们暗示，全球建模并非中立，而是站在那些能够减排——但想让别人帮忙——的富裕国家一边。在1992年里约地球峰会之前的国际谈判中，这一论点足够有说服力，被纳入《联合国气候变化框架公约》。

This north-south separation was one reason anti-environmental politicians in the United States criticized climate change negotiations, and, in the face of international disapproval, withdrew from the Kyoto Protocol in 2001. U.S. politicians have advocated a different form of universals through which they imagine the globe: private property, free trade, and the entrepreneurial spirit. U.S. negotiators had already done their best to bring these business-oriented perspectives into discussions of climate change.
Yet the models of global change that informed climate negotiations still privileged the environment for itself. These environmental universals had not won over U.S. politics.
这种南北分离是美国反环境政治家批评气候变化谈判的原因之一，并且在国际反对声中，他们于2001年退出了《京都议定书》。美国政治家提倡一种不同的普遍性形式，借以想象地球：私有财产、自由贸易和企业家精神。美国谈判代表已经尽力把这些商业导向的视角带入气候变化讨论。
然而，为气候谈判提供信息的全球变化模型仍然为环境本身赋予特权。这些环境普遍性没有赢得美国政界的支持。

U.S. intransigence warns us against the glorification of incompatibility; when claims of difference are combined with unilateral power, they can be ugly. Whereas representatives of the south asked for revisions of the model, the most powerful nation of the north merely refused to discuss it. Powerful blocs have worked hard to stop global agreements based on international cooperation and amity. The expertise of modelers has formed defensive walls against such power plays, but generalizations more directly dependent on international politics have had fewer defenses.
美国的不妥协警告我们不要美化不相容性；当差异的主张与单边权力结合时，它们可能很丑陋。南方代表要求修订模型，而北方最强大的国家只是拒绝讨论它。强大的集团努力阻止基于国际合作与友好的全球协议。建模者的专业知识形成了抵御这种权力游戏的防御墙，但更直接依赖国际政治的概括防御更少。

The recognition of environmental crisis has brought nations to the negotiating table to talk about a variety of universal standards. But not all negotiations result in effective generalization. Negotiators must agree upon common objects. As long as they refuse all compatibility, generalization is impossible. The troubled progress of international negotiations illuminates the specificity of the generalization process, in which productive collaborations and sincerely endorsed axioms of unity are not easy achievements. I turn to these troubles.
对环境危机的认识把各国带到谈判桌前，讨论各种普遍标准。但并非所有谈判都能产生有效的概括。谈判者必须就共同对象达成一致。只要他们拒绝一切相容性，概括就不可能。国际谈判的艰难进展阐明了概括过程的特殊性，在其中，富有成效的合作与真诚认可的统一公理都不是容易的成就。我转向这些困难。

The ITTO’s underlying concept is to sustainable development of tropical forests by encouraging and assisting the tropical timber industry and trade to manage and thus conserve the resource base on which they depend.
ITTO的基本理念，是通过鼓励并协助热带木材产业与贸易部门管理并进而保护它们所依赖的资源基础，实现热带森林的可持续发展。
—International Tropical Timber Organization, “What Is the International Tropical Timber Agreement?”
——国际热带木材组织，《什么是国际热带木材协定？》（“What Is the International Tropical Timber Agreement?”）

The combination of trade promotion and conservation is a heady brew for international politics. Nowhere has this been more important than in the International Tropical Timber Organization, better known as the ITTO. With this combination brewing, the dream of a global management regime was born. Could forest protectors and exploiters, and wood producers and consumers, come together to form universal standards, governance procedures, and expectations about the use of forests?
贸易促进与保护的结合，对国际政治是一杯烈酒。这种结合在国际热带木材组织（以简称ITTO更为人熟知）中尤为重要。随着这种结合开始酿制，全球管理制度之梦诞生了。森林保护者与开发者、木材生产者与消费者，能否走到一起，形成关于森林使用的普遍标准、治理程序和期望？

The ITTO’s hopes for forming universal standards came to life around the concept of “sustainable forest management.” Sustainable management emerged at the intersection of varied concerns about “protection”: of wood supplies for consumer industry; of state forestry institutions; of wood prices for timber companies; of the reputation of the forest-products trade; and, of course, of forests themselves. Sustainable management showed the potential to reshape conservation, trade, forestry, and industry, so that they formed a common trajectory in a commitment to a managed global Nature. Sustainable management could be the cornerstone of a new governmentality. Yet the most exciting thing about the ITTO turned out to be its failure. Everyone saw quickly that “sustainable management” was an empty concept. The ITTO stayed on, but the action, emerging from other sites, swirled around it. The ITTO took up the defensive role of managing participants’ agendas in the light of what was happening elsewhere.

ITTO形成普遍标准的希望围绕“可持续森林管理”概念而活跃起来。可持续管理出现在各种“保护”关切的交汇处：为消费产业保护木材供应；保护国家林业机构；为木材公司保护木材价格；为林产品贸易保护声誉；当然也保护森林本身。可持续管理显示出重塑保护、贸易、林业和工业的潜力，使它们在对被管理的全球自然的承诺中形成共同轨迹。可持续管理可以成为新治理术的基石。然而，ITTO最令人兴奋的事结果却是它的失败。大家很快看出，“可持续管理”是一个空洞的概念。ITTO留了下来，但来自其他场所的行动围绕它旋转。ITTO承担起防御性角色，根据别处正在发生的事情管理参与者的议程。

This section, then, turns from relatively successful agendas for global Nature to consider a relatively unsuccessful one. A coalition politics continues to sustain the ITTO, but it is not a coalition that has forged effective collaborations. Some participants hang in, hoping to exert influence on other players and on international programs. They advocate global accord for the name, not the substance; they are most involved in their separate mandates. In their still-strident efforts, global Nature stutters, and falls silent. Why?
因此，本节从相对成功的全球自然议程转向一个相对不成功的议程。联盟政治继续维持ITTO，但它并不是一个锻造了有效合作的联盟。一些参与者坚持留下，希望对其他行动者和国际项目施加影响。他们倡导全球协议是为了名义，而不是实质；他们最投入于各自的职责目标。在他们仍然尖锐的努力中，全球自然结结巴巴，然后沉默。为什么？

The ITTO was imagined as a forum in which compromises might bridge disagreements among dissimilar parties. Even while claiming to search for common ground, the organization worked assiduously to maintain these globe-ripping divides. The ITTO began as a Japanese dream, suggested to the UN Conference on Trade and Development in 1977. The Japanese representatives said they were concerned about the stability of the tropical timber trade, for which Japan was the most prominent consumer. Conservationists and foresters had pointed to evidence of rapid deforestation; supplies in key Japanese source areas, such as the Philippines, were already running out. The Japanese plan blocked other possibilities. Sporadic discussions among tropical wood producing countries had generated speculation that a cartel might form to influence supply and pricing. It also seemed possible that conservationists, concerned about the rapid loss of tropical forests, might themselves succeed in forming international forestry standards. In either case, Japan's business profits would suffer. These concerns informed several years of discussion of the proposal. In 1983, an International Tropical Timber Agreement (ITTA) was signed, to take effect in 1985. The agreement formalized the dialogue between tropical wood producing countries and consuming countries. It included conservation as well as trade promotion goals. The agreement also formed the ITTO.

ITTO被想象成一个论坛，在其中妥协也许能弥合不同各方之间的分歧。即使在声称寻找共同基础时，该组织也努力维持这些撕裂地球的分歧。ITTO最初是一个日本梦想，于1977年向联合国贸易和发展会议提出。日本代表说，他们担心热带木材贸易的稳定，日本是其中最突出的消费国。环保主义者和林业工作者已经指出快速毁林的证据；日本关键来源地区如菲律宾的供应已日渐枯竭。日本的计划阻止了其他可能性。热带木材生产国之间零星的讨论引发了猜测：可能形成一个卡特尔来影响供应和定价。似乎也有可能的是，担心热带森林迅速丧失的环保主义者自己可能成功形成国际林业标准。无论哪种情况，日本的商业利润都会受损。这些关切为几年间对该提案的讨论提供了信息。1983年，《国际热带木材协定》（ITTA）签署，1985年生效。该协定正式确立了热带木材生产国和消费国之间的对话。它包括保护目标，也包括贸易促进目标。该协定还成立了ITTO。

Bureaucratic structure seems cut and dry; but much agonizing and struggle went into settling the structure of the ITTO. Who would participate? What global, national, or business commitments would dominate the agenda? These were questions hammered out in the organizational structure. The ITTA made a start. The organization would be divided into moities, consisting of representatives of nation-states, and identified respectively as “producers” and “consumers”—thus assuring that the ITTO would function neither as a price-setting cartel nor as a forum for global citizens. Votes were to be distributed in proportion to a nation-state’s “involvement” with the tropical timber trade; countries that either bought or sold more tropical wood received more votes. As one critic points out: “The net result is that the more a country destroys tropical forests, the more votes it gets. The voting structure ensures that the ITTO’s primary role of promoting the timber trade heavily outweighs its secondary conservation role” (Colchester 1990: 167).

These arrangements meant that the struggle over the organization’s goals was played out in relation to the representation of different countries. Forest conservation objectives became identified with countries such as the United Kingdom and the Netherlands; the voice of the wood-products industry was heard from Japan; the defense of national sovereignty and rights to destroy the forests became identified with Indonesia and Malaysia. Thus, too, the struggle over which nation would supply the Executive Director and where the secretariat would be seated was a struggle over organizational definition. The battle was heated. Finally, the Japanese government offered to fund the ITTO in exchange for gaining the secretariat. Japanese support then boosted a Malaysian forester, Dr. Freezailah, to the post of Executive Director (Colchester 1990).

官僚结构似乎明确而固定；但为了确定ITTO的结构，经历了大量痛苦与斗争。谁将参与？哪些全球、国家或商业承诺将主导议程？这些都是在组织结构中锤炼出来的问题。ITTA开了一个头。组织将分为两部分，由民族国家代表组成，分别称为“生产者”和“消费者”——从而确保ITTO既不会作为定价卡特尔运作，也不会作为全球公民的论坛。选票将按民族国家与热带木材贸易的“参与程度”比例分配；买卖更多热带木材的国家获得更多选票。正如一位批评者指出：“净结果是，一个国家破坏热带森林越多，它获得的选票就越多。投票结构确保ITTO促进木材贸易的主要角色大大超过其次要的保护角色”（Colchester 1990: 167）。

这些安排意味着，围绕组织目标的斗争是在不同国家的代表权关系中展开的。森林保护目标与英国、荷兰等国联系在一起；木制品产业的声音从日本发出；捍卫国家主权和毁林权的声音则与印尼和马来西亚联系在一起。因此，围绕哪个国家提供执行主任、秘书处设在哪里的斗争，也是一场关于组织定义的斗争。这场战斗很激烈。最后，日本政府提出资助ITTO以换取秘书处。日本的支持随后把马来西亚林业官员弗里扎伊拉博士推上执行主任的位置（Colchester 1990）。

Despite this alignment of Japanese and Malaysian interests in rapid timber exploitation, conservationists hung on. Getting forest conservation goals into a mandate that had begun as a trade agreement was a victory; they were not about to retreat. For nongovernmental organizations, the goal of participating at all in ITTO negotiations seemed overwhelmingly important. In Indonesia, for example, environmental NGOs were just then struggling for a voice in the nation—in the legal system, in forestry, and in public culture. Indonesia was a major player in the ITTO, and NGOs wanted to be involved.
尽管日本和马来西亚在快速木材开发上的利益如此一致，自然保护者仍坚持下来。把森林保护目标纳入一项最初作为贸易协定的授权，是一场胜利；他们不打算撤退。对非政府组织来说，能够参与ITTO谈判似乎极其重要。例如，在印尼，环境非政府组织当时正努力在国家中获得发言权——在法律系统、林业和公共文化中。印尼是ITTO的主要参与者，非政府组织想要参与。

In other arenas—including global climate change—agreement among experts has sparked intergovernmental cooperation. Not so for forest protection. Experts are differently aligned. Foresters have been trained to work with the timber industry, not the environmental movement; in contrast, conservation biologists, often spokespersons for environmentalism, may oppose logging. Anthropologists, who may speak up for forest-dwelling peoples, are rarely given credence by either foresters or biologists. Economists are given much credence although they may know nothing about forests. Agendas for forest management thus multiply. Most experts adopt a rhetoric of concern for forests, whether they propose to stay or hasten their disappearance. The 1992 UN Earth Summit at Rio produced a set of principles on forests that affirm state sovereignty and promote free trade; what does this have to do with forest protection?
Thus, too, the ITTO combines and juxtaposes agendas that, everyone admits, contradict each other.

在其他领域——包括全球气候变化——专家之间的一致引发了政府间合作。森林保护则不是这样。专家的阵营不同。林业工作者受训与木材产业合作，而不是与环境运动合作；相比之下，保护生物学家常常是环保主义的代言人，可能反对伐木。人类学家可能为森林居民发声，却很少得到林业工作者或生物学家的信任。经济学家得到很多信任，尽管他们可能对森林一无所知。因此，森林管理的议程成倍增加。大多数专家都采用关心森林的修辞，无论他们主张遏止还是加速森林的消失。1992年里约联合国地球峰会产出了一套关于森林的原则，肯定国家主权并促进自由贸易；这与森林保护有什么关系？
因此，ITTO也把大家都承认相互矛盾的议程结合并并置在一起。

Sustainable management holds the mix together. But it is not enough. The ITTO promotes sustainable management of forests. But, given the selfconscious reliance on contradictory programs, it is difficult for the organization to define the term substantively. Here is the organization’s formal definition:
可持续管理把这种混合维系在一起。但这还不够。ITTO促进森林的可持续管理。然而，鉴于自觉依赖相互矛盾的项目，该组织很难实质性定义这个术语。以下是该组织的正式定义：

Sustainable forest management is the process of managing forest to achieve one or more clearly specified objectives of management with regard to the production of a continuous flow of desired forest products and services without undue reduction of the inherent values and future productivity and without undue undesirable effects on the physical and social environment.
可持续森林管理是管理森林的过程，以达到一个或多个明确规定的管理目标，涉及持续产生所需的森林产品和服务，同时不过度减少固有价值和未来生产力，也不对物理和社会环境产生过度的不良影响。

This is obviously a compromise between sustainable yield—the foresters’ dream of stable timber production (“a continuous flow of desired forest products”)—and sustainable ecological function—the environmentalists’ goal (“inherent values,” “undesirable effects”). The product is almost incomprehensible. Furthermore, no one knows how to do it. No one, even industry experts, thinks that current tropical logging techniques are allowing the forest to regenerate—even for timber.
这显然是可持续产量——林业工作者稳定木材生产的梦想（“持续产生所需的森林产品”）——与可持续生态功能——环保主义者的目标（“固有价值”、“不良影响”）——之间的妥协。产物几乎无法理解。此外，没有人知道如何做到。没有人，甚至行业专家，认为当前的热带伐木技术能让森林再生——即使是为了木材。

Two paths present themselves as ways out of this conundrum. One could use the term as public relations rhetoric to defend the reputation of current logging practices, taking them out of the opprobrium of environmentalist criticism. The advantage here is that it doesn’t matter if the definition is incomprehensible. Alternatively, one could focus on management itself as the true objective. By rationalizing data collection and bureaucratic structures for forestry while at the same time highlighting technical training, one might achieve some goals, even if they might not be forest protection ones. After all, the definition says that sustainable management is meeting the specified objectives of management. It is management itself that must be sustainable. The ITTO has worked back and forth between these two paths.

有两条路径可以摆脱这个难题。人们可以把该术语用作公共关系的修辞，以捍卫当前伐木实践的声誉，使其免受环保主义批评的责难。这样做的好处是，定义是否不可理解并不重要。或者，人们可以专注于管理本身作为真正目标。通过使林业的数据收集和官僚结构合理化，同时突出技术培训，人们可能实现某些目标，即使这些目标可能不是森林保护的目标。毕竟，定义说可持续管理就是达到规定的管理目标。必须可持续的是管理本身。ITTO在这两条路径之间来回工作。
